## PDF page 164

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=164)

```text
                    CO OPEN-RAISING


Now you will move over to the CO.

Action folds around to you and you have three players left to act; the BTN,
SB, and BB. You are given the defense range for these players, and will start
by filling out the %-form for each of them. To clarify, filling out the %-form is
not meant to be mindless busy work. The goal is to build your intuition when
it comes to how often a player does something preflop and how that fre-
quency translates into a usable range. Solid preflop hand reading makes
postflop hand reading far more effective.

Then answer the questions below.

You can calculate how often everyone folds by hand, or use my “Multiple
Folders” spreadsheet available at www.splitsuit.pro/sheets

Just like last time, these defense ranges are simplified to make your life easier.
Keep in mind that players implementing a more static strategy are less likely
to veer away from their overall defense ranges. On the other hand, dynamic
players will be more fluid to the exact action, stack sizes, edges, etc.

And once again, notice the outright success rate of both raise sizes.

GLGL.




                                    PA G E 1 6 4
```

## PDF page 166

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=166)

```text
                               CHAPTER FOURTEEN



                               ISOLATING


An isolation raise is a preflop raise made after one or more limpers. While
open-limping is more common in lower stakes games, understanding these
spots from a technical point of view is helpful.

These first exercises will focus on spots where there is a single limper.

TOOLS TO USE: Any range software (Flopzilla, Equilab, PokerCruncher, etc.)
and a calculator. You can calculate how often everyone folds manually, or
use the “Multiple Folders” spreadsheet available at www.splitsuit.pro/sheets

PROCESS: Each page contains a preflop exercise where one player open-
limps and you decide to make an isolation raise. Start by getting the %-form
for the range you assume your opponent open-limped with and also the
range you think they would give your isolation raise action with. Then answer
the questions below.

Remember that your opponent’s folding frequency is

          FOL D % = 10 0 % - (C ON T I N UA NC E R A N G E / OR IG I NA L R A N G E)


So if they originally limped with 20% of hands and would continue with 12% of
hands after you raise, 100%-(12%/20%) = 40%. Which means you can expect
them to fold 40% of the time when you raise their limp.



                                         PA G E 1 6 6
```

## PDF page 167

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=167)

```text
                          I S O L AT I N G: VS . 1 L I M P E R


TAKEAWAYS: Some players will get frustrated that no hole cards are given in
these exercises, but most people get distracted by their cards and miss the
big-picture. If you find a spot where a player is folding a ton of the time when
you isolate, and the players behind you are folding often too, does it matter
much if you hold AKo or Q9s? If you find a spot where players are folding
to isolation raises rarely, are you really going to add many weak hands into
your isolation range?

GLGL.




                                     PA G E 1 6 7
```
